page: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-4g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine tailored for demanding parallel compute workloads. It is equipped with four NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs providing a combined total of 160 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, supplying 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. System memory totals 340 GB of RAM, offering roughly 7.08 GB of memory per vCPU. The CPU features 38 MB of L3 cache along with instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic AES extensions. Local instance storage is not included, requiring external persistent disks or network-attached volumes for data persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution in machine learning and tensor operations driven by the quad-A100 GPU array. In large language model inference, the instance achieves top 10% performance across prompt processing and generation phases, processing 2725.85 tokens per second on medium 7B models and sustaining 449.76 tokens per second during prompt ingestion for large 70B parameter models. Text generation throughput remains robust at 108.33 tokens per second on 7B models and 19.59 tokens per second on 70B models.

By contrast, general-purpose CPU metrics demonstrate moderate to low performance characteristics. Single-core tests reflect lower relative speed, evidenced by bottom-quartile ratings in Geekbench single-core (1062.0), single-core stress-ng (1201.28), and single-threaded gzip compression (20.47 GB/sec). However, multi-core benchmarks scale to mid-tier performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 31203.01 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 10469.0. Memory bandwidth remains balanced for a large host, measuring 109.83 GB/sec on large uncached read operations.

Given its specialized accelerator density, the a2-highgpu-4g offers high resource efficiency for workloads that can fully exploit its GPU memory and multi-device parallelism. It is an effective platform for distributed deep learning training, large language model deployment, high-performance computing, and parallel data science pipelines, whereas standard web serving or CPU-bound single-thread tasks are economically mismatched.
